Main.sentence: Afghanistan , [e] officially the Islamic Emirate of Afghanistan , [f] is a ___E:landlocked country U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Landlocked_country)___ located at the crossroads of ___E:Central U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Central_Asia)___ and ___E:South Asia U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Asia)___ .

It is bordered by ___E:Pakistan U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pakistan)___ to the ___E:east and south U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Durand_Line)___ , [g] ___E:Iran U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Iran)___ to the ___E:west U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Afghanistan%E2%80%93Iran_border)___ , ___E:Turkmenistan U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Turkmenistan)___ to the ___E:northwest U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Afghanistan%E2%80%93Turkmenistan_border)___ , ___E:Uzbekistan U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Uzbekistan)___ to the ___E:north U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Afghanistan%E2%80%93Uzbekistan_border)___ , ___E:Tajikistan U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tajikistan)___ to the ___E:northeast U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Afghanistan%E2%80%93Tajikistan_border)___ , and ___E:China U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/China)___ to the ___E:northeast and east U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Afghanistan%E2%80%93China_border)___ .

Occupying 652,864 square kilometers (252,072 sq mi) of land, the country is predominantly mountainous with plains ___E:in the north U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Afghan_Turkestan)___ and ___E:the southwest U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sistan_Basin)___ , which are separated by the ___E:Hindu Kush U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hindu_Kush)___ mountain range. ___E:Kabul U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kabul)___ is the country's capital and largest city. ___E:Afghanistan's population U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Demographics_of_Afghanistan)___ is estimated to be between 36 and 50 million. [d]

___E:Human habitation in Afghanistan U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ancient_history_of_Afghanistan)___ dates to the ___E:Middle Paleolithic U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Middle_Paleolithic)___ era. Popularly referred to as the ___E:graveyard of empires U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Graveyard_of_empires)___ ,  the land ___E:has witnessed numerous military campaigns U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Invasions_of_Afghanistan)___ , including those by the ___E:Persians U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Persian_empire)___ , ___E:Alexander the Great U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alexander_the_Great)___ , the ___E:Maurya Empire U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maurya_Empire)___ , ___E:Arab Muslims U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Muslim_conquests_of_Afghanistan)___ , the ___E:Mongols U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mongol_invasion_of_the_Khwarazmian_Empire)___ , the ___E:British U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/European_influence_in_Afghanistan#The_Great_Game)___ , the ___E:Soviet Union U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Soviet%E2%80%93Afghan_War)___ , and ___E:a US-led coalition U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/War_in_Afghanistan_(2001%E2%80%932021))___ .

Afghanistan also served as the source from which the ___E:Greco-Bactrians U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Greco-Bactrian_Kingdom)___ and the ___E:Mughals U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mughal_Empire)___ , among others, rose to form major empires.

Because of the various conquests and periods in both the ___E:Iranian U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Greater_Iran)___ and ___E:Indian U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Greater_India)___ cultural spheres,   the area was a center for ___E:Zoroastrianism U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zoroastrianism)___ , ___E:Buddhism U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Buddhism)___ , ___E:Hinduism U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hinduism)___ , and later Islam.

The modern state of Afghanistan began with the ___E:Durrani Afghan Empire U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Durrani_Empire)___ in the 18th century,  although ___E:Dost Mohammad Khan U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dost_Mohammad_Khan)___ is sometimes considered to be the founder of the first ___E:modern Afghan state U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Emirate_of_Afghanistan)___ .

Afghanistan became a ___E:buffer state U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Buffer_state)___ in the ___E:Great Game U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Great_Game)___ between the ___E:British Empire U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/British_Empire)___ and the ___E:Russian Empire U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Russian_Empire)___ .

From India, the British attempted to subjugate Afghanistan but were repelled in the ___E:First Anglo-Afghan War U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/First_Anglo-Afghan_War)___ ; the ___E:Second Anglo-Afghan War U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Second_Anglo-Afghan_War)___ saw a British victory.

Following the ___E:Third Anglo-Afghan War U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Third_Anglo-Afghan_War)___ in 1919, Afghanistan became free of foreign political hegemony, and emerged as the independent ___E:Kingdom of Afghanistan U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kingdom_of_Afghanistan)___ in 1926. This monarchy lasted almost half a century, until ___E:Zahir Shah U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mohammed_Zahir_Shah)___ was ___E:overthrown in 1973 U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1973_Afghan_coup_d%27%C3%A9tat)___ , following which the ___E:Republic of Afghanistan U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Republic_of_Afghanistan_(1973%E2%80%931978))___ was established.

Since the late 1970s, Afghanistan's history has been dominated by extensive warfare, including ___E:coups, invasions, insurgencies, and civil wars U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Afghan_conflict)___ .

The conflict began in 1978 when ___E:a communist revolution U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saur_Revolution)___ established a ___E:socialist state U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Democratic_Republic_of_Afghanistan)___ (itself a response to the dictatorship established following a ___E:coup d'état in 1973 U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1973_Afghan_coup_d%27%C3%A9tat)___ ), and subsequent infighting prompted the ___E:Soviet Union to invade Afghanistan U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Soviet_invasion_of_Afghanistan)___ in 1979. The ___E:mujahideen U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Afghan_mujahideen)___ won against the Soviets in ___E:Soviet–Afghan War U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Soviet%E2%80%93Afghan_War)___ , leading to the ___E:Soviets' withdrawal in 1989 U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Soviet_withdrawal_from_Afghanistan)___ .

The ensuing ___E:civil war U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Afghan_Civil_War_(1989%E2%80%931992))___ overthrew the socialist republic and established the ___E:Islamic State of Afghanistan U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Islamic_State_of_Afghanistan)___ through ___E:Peshawar Accord U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peshawar_Accord)___ , which could not remain in force and resulted in a ___E:second civil war U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Afghan_Civil_War_(1992%E2%80%931996))___ between mujahideen factions in 1992. The ___E:Taliban U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taliban)___ controlled most of the country by 1996, but their ___E:Islamic Emirate of Afghanistan U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Islamic_Emirate_of_Afghanistan_(1996%E2%80%932001))___ received little international recognition before its overthrow in the 2001 ___E:US invasion of Afghanistan U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_invasion_of_Afghanistan)___ .

The Taliban returned to power in 2021 after ___E:capturing Kabul U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fall_of_Kabul_(2021))___ , ending the ___E:2001–2021 war U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/War_in_Afghanistan_(2001%E2%80%932021))___ .

As of July 2025 [update] , the Taliban government is ___E:widely unrecognized U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Recognition_of_the_Islamic_Emirate_of_Afghanistan)___ by the international community due to reported violations of ___E:human rights in Afghanistan U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Human_rights_in_Afghanistan)___ , particularly regarding the rights of ___E:women in Afghanistan U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Women_in_Afghanistan)___ and the ___E:treatment of women by the Taliban U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Treatment_of_women_by_the_Taliban)___ .
Afghanistan is rich in natural resources, including ___E:lithium U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lithium)___ , iron, ___E:zinc U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zinc)___ , and copper.

It is the second-largest producer of ___E:cannabis resin U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cannabis_resin)___ ,  [obsolete source] and third largest of both ___E:saffron U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saffron)___  and ___E:cashmere U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cashmere_wool)___ .

The country is a member of the ___E:South Asian Association for Regional Cooperation U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Asian_Association_for_Regional_Cooperation)___ and a founding member of the ___E:Organization of Islamic Cooperation U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Organization_of_Islamic_Cooperation)___ .
Due to the effects of war in recent decades, the country has dealt with high levels of terrorism, ___E:poverty U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Poverty_in_Afghanistan)___ , and child malnutrition.

Afghanistan remains among the world's ___E:least developed countries U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Least_developed_country)___ , ranking 182nd on the ___E:Human Development Index U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Human_Development_Index)___ .
Afghanistan's gross domestic product (GDP) is $81 billion by ___E:purchasing power parity U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Purchasing_power_parity)___ and $20.1 billion by nominal values.
Per capita, its GDP is among the lowest of any country as of 2020 [update] .

Some scholars suggest that the ___E:root U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Root_(linguistics))___ name ___E:Afghān U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Afghan_(ethnonym))___ is derived from the ___E:Sanskrit U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sanskrit)___ word Aśvakan , which was the name used for ancient inhabitants of the ___E:Hindu Kush U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hindu_Kush)___ .

Aśvakan literally means "horsemen", "horse breeders", or " ___E:cavalrymen U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cavalry)___ " (from aśva , the ___E:Sanskrit U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sanskrit)___ and ___E:Avestan U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Avestan)___ words for "horse").
Historically, the ethnonym Afghān was used to refer to ethnic ___E:Pashtuns U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pashtuns)___ .
The Arabic and Persian form of the name, Afġān , was first attested in the 10th-century geography book Hudud al-'Alam .
The last part of the name, " -stan ", is a Persian suffix meaning "place of".
Therefore, "Afghanistan" translates to "land of the Afghans", or "land of the Pashtuns" in a historical sense.
According to the third edition of the Encyclopaedia of Islam :

The name Afghanistan (Afghānistān, land of the Afghans / Pashtuns, afāghina , sing. afghān ) can be traced to the early eighth/fourteenth century, when it designated the easternmost part of the ___E:Kartid U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kartid)___ realm.

This name was later used for certain regions in the ___E:Ṣafavid U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Safavid_Iran)___ and ___E:Mughal U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mughal_Empire)___ empires that were inhabited by Afghans.

While based on a state-supporting elite of ___E:Abdālī / Durrānī U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Durrani)___ Afghans, the ___E:Sadūzāʾī Durrānī polity U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Durrani_Empire)___ that came into being in 1160 / 1747 was not called Afghanistan in its own day. The name became a state designation only during the colonial intervention of the nineteenth century.

The term "Afghanistan" was officially used in 1855, when the British recognized ___E:Dost Mohammad Khan U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dost_Mohammad_Khan)___ as king of ___E:Afghanistan U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Emirate_of_Afghanistan)___ .
Excavations of prehistoric sites suggest that humans were living in what is now Afghanistan at least 50,000 years ago, and that farming communities in the area were among the earliest in the world.
An important site of early historical activities, many believe that Afghanistan compares to ___E:Egypt U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Egypt)___ in the historical value of its archaeological sites.

Artifacts typical of the ___E:Paleolithic U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paleolithic)___ , ___E:Mesolithic U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mesolithic)___ , ___E:Neolithic U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neolithic)___ , ___E:Bronze U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bronze_Age)___ , and ___E:Iron Ages U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Iron_Age)___ have been found in Afghanistan.

Urban civilization is believed to have begun as early as 3000 BCE, and the early city of ___E:Mundigak U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mundigak)___ (near ___E:Kandahar U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kandahar)___ in the south of the country) was a center of the ___E:Helmand culture U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Helmand_culture)___ .
More recent findings established that the ___E:Indus Valley Civilization U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indus_Valley_Civilization)___ stretched up towards modern-day Afghanistan.
An Indus Valley site has been found on the ___E:Oxus River U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oxus_River)___ at ___E:Shortugai U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shortugai)___ in northern Afghanistan.

After 2000 BCE successive waves of semi-nomadic people from Central Asia began moving south into Afghanistan; among them were many ___E:Indo-European U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indo-European_languages)___ -speaking ___E:Indo-Iranians U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indo-Iranians)___ .
These tribes later migrated further into South Asia, Western Asia, and toward Europe via the area north of the ___E:Caspian Sea U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Caspian_Sea)___ .
The region at the time was referred to as ___E:Ariana U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ariana)___ .

By the middle of the 6th century BCE, the Achaemenids overthrew the ___E:Medes U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Medes)___ and incorporated ___E:Arachosia U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arachosia)___ , ___E:Aria U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aria_(satrapy))___ , and ___E:Bactria U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bactria)___ within its eastern boundaries.

An ___E:inscription U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Epigraphy)___ on the tombstone of ___E:Darius I of Persia U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Darius_I_of_Persia)___ mentions the ___E:Kabul Valley U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kabulistan)___ in a list of the 29 countries that he had conquered.

The region of ___E:Arachosia U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arachosia)___ , around ___E:Kandahar U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kandahar)___ in modern-day southern Afghanistan, used to be primarily Zoroastrian and played a key role in the transfer of the Avesta to ___E:Persia U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Persis)___ and is thus considered by some to be the "second homeland of Zoroastrianism".

___E:Alexander the Great U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alexander_the_Great)___ and his Macedonian forces arrived in Afghanistan in 330 BCE after defeating ___E:Darius III of Persia U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Darius_III_of_Persia)___ a year earlier in the ___E:Battle of Gaugamela U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Battle_of_Gaugamela)___ .

Following Alexander's brief occupation, the successor state of the ___E:Seleucid Empire U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seleucid_Empire)___ controlled the region until 305 BCE, when they gave much of it to the ___E:Maurya Empire U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maurya_Empire)___ as part of an alliance treaty.

The Mauryans controlled the area south of the ___E:Hindu Kush U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hindu_Kush)___ until they were overthrown in about 185 BCE. Their decline began 60 years after ___E:Ashoka U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ashoka)___ 's rule ended, leading to the ___E:Hellenistic U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hellenistic)___ reconquest by the ___E:Greco-Bactrians U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Greco-Bactrians)___ .
Much of it soon broke away and became part of the ___E:Indo-Greek Kingdom U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indo-Greek_Kingdom)___ .

They were defeated and expelled by the ___E:Indo-Scythians U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indo-Scythians)___ in the late 2nd century BCE.   The ___E:Silk Road U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Silk_Road)___ appeared during the first century BCE, and Afghanistan flourished with trade, with routes to China, India, Persia, and north to the cities of ___E:Bukhara U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bukhara)___ , ___E:Samarkand U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Samarkand)___ , and ___E:Khiva U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Khiva)___ in present-day Uzbekistan.

Goods and ideas were exchanged at this center point, such as Chinese silk, Persian silver and Roman gold, while the region of present Afghanistan was mining and trading ___E:lapis lazuli U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lapis_lazuli)___ stones  mainly from the ___E:Badakhshan U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Badakhshan)___ region.

During the first century BCE, the ___E:Parthian Empire U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Parthian_Empire)___ subjugated the region but lost it to their ___E:Indo-Parthian U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indo-Parthian)___ vassals.

In the mid-to-late first century CE the vast ___E:Kushan Empire U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kushan_Empire)___ , centered in Afghanistan, became great patrons of Buddhist culture, making ___E:Buddhism U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Buddhism)___ flourish throughout the region.

The Kushans were overthrown by the ___E:Sassanids U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sassanids)___ in the 3rd century CE, though the ___E:Indo-Sassanids U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indo-Sassanids)___ continued to rule at least parts of the region.
They were followed by the ___E:Kidarites U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kidarite)___ who, in turn, was replaced by the ___E:Hephthalites U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hephthalites)___ .
They were replaced by the ___E:Turk Shahi U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Turk_Shahi)___ in the 7th century.

The Buddhist Turk Shahi of Kabul was replaced by a Hindu dynasty before the Saffarids conquered the area in 870, this Hindu dynasty was called ___E:Hindu Shahi U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hindu_Shahi)___ .
Much of the northeastern and southern areas of the country remained dominated by ___E:Buddhist U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Buddhist)___ culture.

___E:Arab U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arab)___ ___E:Muslims U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Muslim)___ brought Islam to ___E:Herat U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Herat)___ and ___E:Zaranj U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zaranj)___ in 642 CE and began spreading eastward; some of the native inhabitants they encountered accepted it while others revolted.

Before the ___E:arrival of Islam U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Islamic_conquest_of_Afghanistan)___ , the region used to be home to various beliefs and cults, often resulting in ___E:Syncretism U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Syncretism)___ between the dominant religions   such as ___E:Zoroastrianism U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zoroastrianism)___ ,    ___E:Buddhism U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Buddhism)___ or ___E:Greco-Buddhism U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Greco-Buddhism)___ , ___E:Ancient Iranian religions U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ancient_Iranian_religion)___ ,  ___E:Hinduism U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hinduism)___ , Christianity,   and Judaism.

An exemplification of the syncretism in the region would be that people were patrons of Buddhism but still worshipped local Iranian gods such as ___E:Ahura Mazda U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ahura_Mazda)___ , ___E:Lady Nana U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nana_(Kushan_goddess))___ , ___E:Anahita U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anahita)___ or ___E:Mihr (Mithra) U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mithra)___ and portrayed ___E:Greek gods U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Greek_mythology)___ as protectors of Buddha.

The ___E:Zunbils U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zunbils)___ and Kabul Shahi were first conquered in 870 CE by the ___E:Saffarid U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saffarid_dynasty)___ Muslims of Zaranj.

Later, the ___E:Samanids U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Samanids)___ extended their Islamic influence south of the Hindu Kush. The ___E:Ghaznavids U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ghaznavids)___ rose to power in the 10th century.

By the 11th century, ___E:Mahmud of Ghazni U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mahmud_of_Ghazni)___ had defeated the remaining Hindu rulers and effectively ___E:Islamized U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Islamized)___ the wider region,  with the exception of ___E:Kafiristan U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kafiristan)___ .

Mahmud made ___E:Ghazni U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ghazni)___ into an important city and patronized intellectuals such as the historian ___E:Al-Biruni U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Al-Biruni)___ and the poet ___E:Ferdowsi U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ferdowsi)___ .

The ___E:Ghaznavid dynasty U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ghaznavid_dynasty)___ was ___E:overthrown by the Ghurids in 1186 U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Siege_of_Lahore_(1186))___ , whose architectural achievements included the remote ___E:Minaret of Jam U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Minaret_of_Jam)___ .
The Ghurids controlled Afghanistan for less than a century before being conquered by the ___E:Khwarazmian dynasty U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Khwarazmian_dynasty)___ in 1215.

In 1219 CE, ___E:Genghis Khan U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Genghis_Khan)___ and his ___E:Mongol army overran the region U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mongol_invasion_of_the_Khwarazmian_Empire)___ .

Similar development projects have also begun in ___E:Herat U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Herat)___ , ___E:Mazar-e-Sharif U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mazar-e-Sharif)___ , and other cities.
An estimated 400,000 people enter the labor market each year.

Several small companies and factories began operating in different parts of the country, which not only provide revenues to the government but also create new jobs. Improvements to the business environment have resulted in more than $1.5 billion in ___E:telecom U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Telecommunications)___ investment and created more than 100,000 jobs since 2003.  ___E:Afghan rugs U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Afghan_rug)___ are becoming popular again, allowing many carpet dealers around the country to hire more workers; in 2016–17 it was the fourth most exported group of items.

Afghanistan is a member of ___E:WTO U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/WTO)___ , ___E:SAARC U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SAARC)___ , ___E:ECO U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Economic_Cooperation_Organization)___ , and ___E:OIC U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/OIC)___ .
It holds an observer status in ___E:SCO U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shanghai_Cooperation_Organisation)___ .
In 2018, a majority of imports come from either Iran, China, Pakistan and Kazakhstan, while 84% of exports are to Pakistan and India.

Since the Taliban's takeover of the country in August 2021, the United States has ___E:frozen about $9 billion U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Afghan_frozen_assets)___ in assets belonging to the ___E:Afghan central bank U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Da_Afghanistan_Bank)___ ,  blocking the Taliban from accessing billions of dollars held in US bank accounts.
The ___E:GDP of Afghanistan U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Economy_of_Afghanistan)___ is estimated to have dropped by 20% following the Taliban return to power.

Following this, after months of free-fall, the Afghan economy began stabilizing, as a result of the Taliban's restrictions on smuggled imports, limits on banking transactions, and ___E:UN aid U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Foreign_aid_to_Afghanistan)___ .
In 2023, the Afghan economy began seeing signs of revival.
This has also been followed by stable exchange rates, low inflation, stable revenue collection, and the rise of trade in exports.

In the third quarter of 2023, the ___E:Afghani U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Afghan_afghani)___ rose to be the best performing currency in the world, climbing over 9% against the ___E:US dollar U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_dollar)___ .

Agricultural production is the backbone of Afghanistan's economy  and has traditionally dominated the economy, employing about 40% of the workforce as of 2018.  The country is known for producing ___E:pomegranates U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pomegranate_production_in_Afghanistan)___ , grapes, apricots, melons, and several other fresh and dry fruits.

Afghanistan also became the world's top producer of ___E:cannabis U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cannabis)___ in 2010.  In March 2023, however, cannabis production was banned by a decree from Hibatullah Akhundzada.
___E:Saffron U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saffron)___ , the most expensive spice, grows in Afghanistan, particularly ___E:Herat Province U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Herat_Province)___ .
In recent years, there has been an uptick in saffron production, which authorities and farmers are using to try to replace poppy cultivation.
Between 2012 and 2019, the saffron cultivated and produced in Afghanistan was consecutively ranked the world's best by the International Taste and Quality Institute.
Production hit record high in 2019 (19,469 kg of saffron), and one kilogram is sold domestically between $634 and $1147.

The availability of cheap diesel-powered water pumps imported from China and Pakistan, and in the 2010s, of cheap solar power to pump water, resulted in expansion of agriculture and population in the southwestern deserts of Afghanistan in ___E:Kandahar U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kandahar_Province)___ , ___E:Helmand U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Helmand_Province)___ and ___E:Nimruz U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nimruz_Province)___ provinces in the 2010s.
Wells have gradually been deepened, but water resources are limited.
Opium is the major crop, but as of 2022, was under attack by the new Taliban government which, to suppress opium production, was systematically suppressing water pumping.
In a 2023 report, poppy cultivation in southern Afghanistan was reduced by over 80% as a result of Taliban campaigns to stop its use toward opium.
This included a 99% reduction of opium growth in the ___E:Helmand Province U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Helmand_Province)___ .
In November 2023, a U.N report showed that in the entirety of Afghanistan, poppy cultivation dropped by over 95%, removing it from its place as being the world's largest opium producer.

The country's natural resources include: coal, copper, iron ore, ___E:lithium U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lithium)___ , ___E:uranium U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Uranium)___ , ___E:rare earth elements U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rare_earth_element)___ , ___E:chromite U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chromite)___ , gold, ___E:zinc U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zinc)___ , ___E:talc U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Talc)___ , ___E:barite U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barite)___ , ___E:sulfur U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sulfur)___ , lead, ___E:marble U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marble)___ , precious and ___E:semi-precious stones U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Semi-precious_stones)___ , natural gas, and petroleum.

In 2010, US and Afghan government officials estimated that untapped mineral deposits located in 2007 by the ___E:US Geological Survey U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/US_Geological_Survey)___ are worth at least $1 trillion .

___E:Michael E. O'Hanlon U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michael_E._O%27Hanlon)___ of the ___E:Brookings Institution U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brookings_Institution)___ estimated that if Afghanistan generates about $10 billion per year from its ___E:mineral deposits U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mining_in_Afghanistan)___ , its ___E:gross national product U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gross_national_product)___ would double and provide long-term funding for critical needs.

The ___E:United States Geological Survey U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Geological_Survey)___ (USGS) estimated in 2006 that northern Afghanistan has an average 460 million m 3 (2.9 billion bbl) of ___E:crude oil U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crude_oil)___ , 440 billion m 3 (15.7 trillion cu ft) of natural gas, and 67 billion L (562 million US bbl) of ___E:natural gas liquids U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Natural_gas_liquids)___ .

In 2011, Afghanistan signed an oil exploration contract with ___E:China National Petroleum Corporation U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/China_National_Petroleum_Corporation)___ (CNPC) for the development of three oil fields along the Amu Darya river in the north.

The country has significant amounts of ___E:lithium U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lithium)___ , copper, gold, coal, iron ore, and other ___E:minerals U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Minerals)___ .

The ___E:Khanashin U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Khanashin)___ ___E:carbonatite U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carbonatite)___ in Helmand Province contains 1,000,000 tonnes (980,000 ___E:long tons U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Long_ton)___ ; 1,100,000 ___E:short tons U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Short_ton)___ ) of ___E:rare earth elements U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rare_earth_element)___ .

In 2007, a 30-year lease was granted for the ___E:Aynak U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mes_Aynak#Copper_Mine)___ copper mine to the ___E:China Metallurgical Group U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/China_Metallurgical_Group)___ for $3 billion,  making it the biggest foreign investment and private business venture in Afghanistan's history.

The state-run ___E:Steel Authority of India U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steel_Authority_of_India)___ won the mining rights to develop the huge ___E:Hajigak U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hajigak_Pass)___ iron ore deposit in central Afghanistan.
Government officials estimate that 30% of the country's untapped mineral deposits are worth at least $1 trillion .
One official asserted that "this will become the backbone of the Afghan economy" and a Pentagon memo stated that Afghanistan could become the "Saudi Arabia of lithium".

The lithium reserves of 21 Mio. tons could amount to the ones of ___E:Bolivia U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bolivia)___ , which is currently viewed as the country with the largest lithium reserves.
Other larger deposits are the ones of ___E:bauxite U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bauxite)___ and ___E:cobalt U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cobalt)___ .
Access to ___E:biocapacity U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Biocapacity)___ in Afghanistan is lower than world average.
In 2016, Afghanistan had 0.43 global hectares  of biocapacity per person within its territory, much less than the world average of 1.6 global hectares per person.
In 2016 Afghanistan used 0.73 global hectares of biocapacity per person—their ___E:ecological footprint U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ecological_footprint)___ of consumption.
This means they use just under double as much biocapacity as Afghanistan contains.
As a result, Afghanistan is running a biocapacity deficit.

In September 2023, the ___E:Taliban U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taliban)___ signed mining contracts worth $6.5 billion , with extractions based on gold, iron, lead, and zinc in the provinces of Herat, Ghor, Logar, and Takhar.

According to the ___E:World Bank U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_Bank)___ , 98% of the rural population have access to electricity in 2018, up from 28% in 2008.  Overall the figure stands at 98.7%.

As of 2016, Afghanistan produces 1,400 ___E:megawatts U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Megawatt)___ of power, but still imports the majority of electricity via transmission lines from Iran and the Central Asian states.
The majority of electricity production is via ___E:hydropower U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hydropower)___ , helped by the amount of rivers and streams that flow from the mountains.
However electricity is not always reliable and blackouts happen, including in Kabul.

In recent years an increasing number of ___E:solar U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Solar_power)___ , ___E:biomass U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Biomass)___ and wind power plants have been constructed.

Currently under development are the ___E:CASA-1000 U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CASA-1000)___ project which will transmit electricity from Kyrgyzstan and Tajikistan, and the ___E:Turkmenistan-Afghanistan-Pakistan-India U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Turkmenistan-Afghanistan-Pakistan-India_pipeline)___ (TAPI) gas pipeline.

Power is managed by the ___E:Da Afghanistan Breshna Sherkat U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Da_Afghanistan_Breshna_Sherkat&action=edit&redlink=1)___ (DABS, Afghanistan Electricity Company).

Important dams include the ___E:Kajaki Dam U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kajaki_Dam)___ , ___E:Dahla Dam U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dahla_Dam)___ , and the ___E:Sardeh Band Dam U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sardeh_Band_Dam)___ .
Tourism is a small industry in Afghanistan due to security issues.

Nevertheless, some 20,000 foreign tourists visit the country annually as of 2016.  In particular an important region for domestic and international tourism is the picturesque ___E:Bamyan U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bamyan)___ Valley, which includes lakes, canyons and historical sites, helped by the fact it is in a safe area away from insurgent activity.
Smaller numbers visit and trek in regions such as the ___E:Wakhan U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wakhan)___ Valley, which is also one of the world's most remote communities.
From the late 1960s onwards, Afghanistan was a popular stop on the famous ___E:hippie trail U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hippie_trail)___ , attracting many Europeans and Americans.

Coming from Iran, the trail traveled through various Afghan provinces and cities including ___E:Herat U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Herat)___ , ___E:Kandahar U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kandahar)___ and ___E:Kabul U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kabul)___ before crossing to northern Pakistan, northern India, and ___E:Nepal U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nepal)___ .
Tourism peaked in 1977, the year before the start of political instability and armed conflict.

The city of ___E:Ghazni U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ghazni)___ has significant history and historical sites, and together with ___E:Bamyan U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bamyan)___ city have in recent years been voted Islamic Cultural Capital and South Asia Cultural Capital respectively.

The cities of ___E:Herat U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Herat)___ , ___E:Kandahar U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kandahar)___ , ___E:Balkh U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Balkh)___ , and ___E:Zaranj U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zaranj)___ are also very historic.

The ___E:Minaret of Jam U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Minaret_of_Jam)___ in the ___E:Hari River U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hari_River,_Afghanistan)___ valley is a ___E:UNESCO World Heritage Site U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UNESCO_World_Heritage_Site)___ .

A cloak reputedly worn by Islam's prophet ___E:Muhammad U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Muhammad)___ is kept in the ___E:Shrine of the Cloak U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shrine_of_the_Cloak)___ in Kandahar, a city founded by ___E:Alexander the Great U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alexander_the_Great)___ and the first capital of Afghanistan.
The ___E:citadel of Alexander U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Citadel_of_Alexander)___ in the western city of Herat has been renovated in recent years and is a popular attraction.

In the north of the country is the ___E:Shrine of Ali U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shrine_of_Ali)___ , believed by many to be the location where ___E:Ali U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ali)___ was buried.

The ___E:National Museum of Afghanistan U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Museum_of_Afghanistan)___ in Kabul hosts a large number of Buddhist, ___E:Bactrian U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bactria)___ Greek and early Islamic antiquities; the museum suffered greatly by civil war but has been slowly restoring since the early 2000s.
Unexpectedly, tourism has seen improvement in Afghanistan following the Taliban takeover.

Active efforts by the Taliban encouraged tourism to increase from 691 tourists in 2021, to 2,300 in 2022, to 5,200 in 2023, with some estimates of between 7,000 and 10,000.    This is, however, threatened by the ___E:Islamic State – Khorasan Province U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Islamic_State_%E2%80%93_Khorasan_Province)___ , who took responsibility for attacks on tourists, such as the ___E:2024 Bamyan shooting U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_Bamyan_shooting)___ .

Telecommunication services in Afghanistan are provided by ___E:Afghan Telecom U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Afghan_Telecom)___ , ___E:Afghan Wireless U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Afghan_Wireless)___ , ___E:Etisalat U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Etisalat)___ , ___E:MTN Group U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MTN_Group)___ , and ___E:Roshan U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roshan_(telco))___ .

The country uses its own space ___E:satellite U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Satellite)___ called ___E:Afghansat 1 U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Afghansat_1)___ , which provides services to millions of phone, internet, and television subscribers.

By 2001 following years of civil war, telecommunications was virtually a non-existent sector, but by 2016 it had grown to a $2 billion industry, with 22 million mobile phone subscribers and 5 million internet users.
The sector employs at least 120,000 people nationwide.
Due to Afghanistan's geography, transport between various parts of the country has historically been difficult.

The backbone of Afghanistan's road network is ___E:Highway 1 U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Highway_1_(Afghanistan))___ , often called the "Ring Road", which extends for 2,210 kilometres (1,370 mi) and connects five major cities: Kabul, Ghazni, Kandahar, Herat and Mazar-i-Sharif,  with spurs to Kunduz and Jalalabad and various border crossings, while skirting around the mountains of the Hindu Kush.
The Ring Road is crucially important for domestic and international trade and the economy.

A key portion of the Ring Road is the ___E:Salang Tunnel U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Salang_Tunnel)___ , completed in 1964, which facilitates travel through the Hindu Kush mountain range and connects northern and southern Afghanistan.
It is the only land route that connects Central Asia to the ___E:Indian subcontinent U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian_subcontinent)___ .
Several mountain passes allow travel between the Hindu Kush in other areas.

Serious traffic accidents are common on Afghan roads and highways, particularly on the ___E:Kabul–Kandahar U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kabul%E2%80%93Kandahar_Highway)___ and the ___E:Kabul–Jalalabad Road U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kabul%E2%80%93Jalalabad_Road)___ .
Traveling by bus in Afghanistan remains dangerous due to militant activities.

Air transport in Afghanistan is provided by the national carrier, ___E:Ariana Afghan Airlines U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ariana_Afghan_Airlines)___ ,  and by the private company ___E:Kam Air U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kam_Air)___ .
Airlines from a number of countries also provide flights in and out of the country.

These include ___E:Air India U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Air_India)___ , ___E:Emirates U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Emirates_(airline))___ , ___E:Gulf Air U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gulf_Air)___ , ___E:Iran Aseman Airlines U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Iran_Aseman_Airlines)___ , ___E:Pakistan International Airlines U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pakistan_International_Airlines)___ , and ___E:Turkish Airlines U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Turkish_Airlines)___ .

The country has four international airports: ___E:Kabul International Airport U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kabul_International_Airport)___ (formerly Hamid Karzai International Airport), ___E:Kandahar International Airport U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kandahar_International_Airport)___ , ___E:Herat International Airport U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Herat_International_Airport)___ , and ___E:Mazar-e Sharif International Airport U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mazar-e_Sharif_International_Airport)___ .
Including domestic airports, there are 43.  ___E:Bagram Air Base U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bagram_Air_Base)___ is a major military airfield.

The country has three rail links: one, a 75-kilometre (47 mi) line from ___E:Mazar-i-Sharif U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mazar-i-Sharif)___ to the ___E:Uzbekistan border U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Afghanistan%E2%80%93Uzbekistan_Friendship_Bridge)___ ;  a 10-kilometre (6.2 mi) long line from ___E:Toraghundi U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Toraghundi)___ to the ___E:Turkmenistan U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Turkmenistan)___ border (where it continues as part of ___E:Turkmen Railways U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Turkmen_Railways)___ ); and a short link from ___E:Aqina U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aqina)___ across the Turkmen border to ___E:Kerki U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kerki)___ , which is planned to be extended further across Afghanistan.
These lines are used for freight only and there is no passenger service.

A rail line between ___E:Khaf U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Khaf,_Iran)___ , Iran and ___E:Herat U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Herat)___ , western Afghanistan, intended for both freight and passengers, was under construction as of 2019.   About 125 kilometres (78 mi) of the line will lie on the Afghan side.
Private vehicle ownership has increased substantially since the early 2000s.
Taxis are yellow and consist of both cars and ___E:auto rickshaws U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Auto_rickshaw)___ .
In rural Afghanistan, villagers often use donkeys, ___E:mules U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mule)___ or horses to transport or carry goods.
Camels are primarily used by the Kochi nomads.
Bicycles are popular throughout Afghanistan.

The population of Afghanistan was estimated at 35.7 million as of 2024 by the Afghanistan ___E:National Statistics and Information Authority U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Statistics_and_Information_Authority)___ ,  whereas the UN estimates over 42.0 million.
In 1979 the total population was reported to be about 15.5 million.
About 25.3% are ___E:urbanite U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Urban_area)___ , 70.4% live in rural areas, and the remaining 4.3% are nomadic.

An additional 3 million or so Afghans are temporarily housed in neighboring ___E:Pakistan U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Afghans_in_Pakistan)___ and ___E:Iran U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Afghans_in_Iran)___ , most of whom were born and raised in those two countries.
As of 2013, Afghanistan was the largest refugee-producing country in the world, a title held for 32 years.
The current population growth rate is 2.37%,  one of the highest in the world outside of Africa.
This population is expected to reach 82 million by 2050 if current population trends continue.
The population of Afghanistan increased steadily until the 1980s, when civil war caused millions to flee to other countries such as Pakistan.
Millions have since returned and the war conditions contribute to the country having the highest fertility rate outside Africa.

Afghanistan's healthcare has recovered since the turn of the century, causing falls in infant mortality and increases in life expectancy, although it has the lowest life expectance of any country outside Africa.

This (along with other factors such as returning refugees) caused rapid population growth in the 2000s that has only recently started to slow down. [citation needed] The ___E:Gini coefficient U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gini_coefficient)___ in 2008 was 27.8.

Afghanistan 2024 ___E:total fertility rate U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Total_fertility_rate)___ has been estimated at 4.4.  In 2022 it was 4.5, about twice the world average rate.  The rate has fallen since the early 1980s.

As estimated by the CIA World Factbook, 26% of the population was urbanized as of 2020. This is one of the lowest figures in the world; in Asia it is only higher than ___E:Cambodia U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cambodia)___ , ___E:Nepal U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nepal)___ and ___E:Sri Lanka U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sri_Lanka)___ .

Urbanization has increased rapidly, particularly in the capital ___E:Kabul U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kabul)___ , due to returning refugees from Pakistan and Iran after 2001, internally displaced people, and rural migrants.
Urbanization in Afghanistan is different from typical urbanization in that it is centered on just a few cities.
Kabul is the largest city, with a population of 5 million.

The other large cities are located generally in the "ring" around the Central Highlands, namely ___E:Kandahar U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kandahar)___ in the south, ___E:Herat U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Herat)___ in the west, ___E:Mazar-i-Sharif U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mazar-i-Sharif)___ , ___E:Kunduz U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kunduz)___ in the north, and ___E:Jalalabad U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jalalabad)___ in the east.
___E:Afghans U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Afghans)___ are divided into several ___E:ethnolinguistic U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ethnolinguistic_group)___ groups.

According to research data by several institutions in 2019, the ___E:Pashtuns U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pashtuns)___ are the largest ethnic group, comprising 42%, followed by ___E:Tajiks U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tajiks)___ , comprising 27%     of the country's population.
The other two major ethnic groups are the ___E:Hazaras U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hazaras)___ and ___E:Uzbeks U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Uzbeks)___ , each at 9%.
A further 10 other ethnic groups are recognized and each are represented in the ___E:Afghan National Anthem U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Afghan_National_Anthem)___ .

___E:Dari U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dari)___ and ___E:Pashto U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pashto)___ are the ___E:official languages U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Official_language)___ of Afghanistan; ___E:bilingualism U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bilingualism)___ is very common.

Dari, which is also referred to as Eastern Persian as it is a variety of and mutually intelligible with ___E:Persian U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Persian_language)___ (and very often called ' ___E:Farsi U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Farsi)___ ' by some Afghans like in ___E:Iran U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Iran)___ ), functions as the ___E:lingua franca U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lingua_franca)___ in Kabul as well as in much of the northern and northwestern parts of the country.
Native speakers of Dari, of any ethnicity, are sometimes called ___E:Farsiwans U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Farsiwan)___ .
Pashto is the native tongue of the ___E:Pashtuns U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pashtuns)___ , although many of them are also fluent in Dari while some non-Pashtuns are fluent in Pashto.
Despite the Pashtuns having been dominant in Afghan politics for centuries, Dari remained the preferred language for government and bureaucracy.

According to ___E:CIA World Factbook U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_World_Factbook)___ , Dari Persian is spoken by 78% ( ___E:L1 U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/First_language)___ + ___E:L2 U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Second_language)___ ) and functions as the lingua franca, while ___E:Pashto U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pashto)___ is spoken by 50%, ___E:Uzbek U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Uzbek_language)___ 10%, English 5%, ___E:Turkmen U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Turkmen_language)___ 2%, ___E:Urdu U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Urdu)___ 2%, ___E:Pashayi U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pashayi_languages)___ 1%, ___E:Nuristani U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nuristani_languages)___ 1%, ___E:Arabic U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arabic)___ 1%, and ___E:Balochi U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Balochi_language)___ 1% (2021 est).

___E:Afghans U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Afghans)___ have both common cultural features and those that differ between the regions of Afghanistan, each with distinctive cultures partly as a result of geographic obstacles that divide the country.
Family is the mainstay of Afghan society and families are often headed by a ___E:patriarch U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Patriarch)___ .

In the southern and eastern region, the people live according to the ___E:Pashtun culture U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pashtun_culture)___ by following ___E:Pashtunwali U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pashtunwali)___ (the Pashtun way).

Key tenets of Pashtunwali include ___E:hospitality U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Melmastia)___ , the provision of ___E:sanctuary U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nanawatai)___ to those seeking refuge, and revenge for the shedding of blood.

Some non-Pashtuns who live in proximity with Pashtuns have adopted Pashtunwali in a process called ___E:Pashtunization U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pashtunization)___ , while some Pashtuns have been ___E:Persianized U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Persianized)___ .

The Afghan people are known to be strongly religious.
Afghans, particularly Pashtuns, are noted for their tribal solidarity and high regard for personal honor.
There are various ___E:Afghan tribes U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ethnic_groups_in_Afghanistan)___ , and an estimated 2–3 million ___E:nomads U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kochi_people)___ .

Afghan culture is deeply ___E:Islamic U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Islamic_culture)___ ,  but pre-Islamic practices persist.  ___E:Child marriage U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Child_marriage_in_Afghanistan)___ is prevalent;  the legal age for marriage is 16.  The most preferred marriage in Afghan society is to one's ___E:parallel cousin U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Parallel_cousin)___ , and the groom is often expected to pay a ___E:bride price U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bride_price)___ .

In the villages, families typically occupy ___E:mudbrick U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mudbrick)___ houses, or compounds with mudbrick or ___E:stone walled U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stone_wall)___ houses.
Villages typically have a headman ( malik ), a master for water distribution ( mirab ) and a religious teacher ( mullah ).
Men would typically work on the fields, joined by women during harvest.
About 15% of the population are ___E:nomadic U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nomadic)___ , locally called kochis .

When nomads pass villages they often buy supplies such as tea, wheat and ___E:kerosene U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kerosene)___ from the villagers; villagers buy ___E:wool U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wool)___ and milk from the nomads.

___E:Afghan clothing U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Afghan_clothing)___ for both men and women typically consists of various forms of ___E:shalwar kameez U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shalwar_kameez)___ , especially perahan tunban and khet partug .
Women would normally wear a chador for head covering; some women, typically from highly conservative communities, wear the burqa , a full body covering.

These were worn by some women of the Pashtun community well before Islam came to the region, but the ___E:Taliban U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taliban)___ enforced this dress on women when they were in power.
Another popular dress is the chapan which acts as a coat. The karakul is a hat made from the fur of a specific regional breed of sheep.

It was favored by former kings of Afghanistan and became known to much of the world in the 21st century when it was constantly worn by President ___E:Hamid Karzai U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hamid_Karzai)___ .

The pakol is another traditional hat originating from the far east of the country; it was popularly worn by the guerrilla leader ___E:Ahmad Shah Massoud U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ahmad_Shah_Massoud)___ .

The nation has a complex history that has survived either in its current cultures or in the form of various languages and monuments.

Afghanistan contains many remnants from all ages, including ___E:Greek U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ancient_Greece)___ and ___E:Buddhist U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Buddhist)___ stupas, monasteries, monuments, temples, and Islamic minarets.

___E:Pottery U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pottery)___ has been crafted in Afghanistan for millennia.

___E:Khushal Khan Khattak U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Khushal_Khan_Khattak)___ of the 17th century is considered the national poet.
